rising.description: Open-source, local-first social media research agent for Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn. Jev routes read-only steps; socai CLI captures cited browser evidence.

strengths: Local-first design with read-only operations and documented data flow
Produces source-cited reports with recorded example output
Open source with a tests badge and a stated release version

Profile and comment extraction could be used to build dossiers on individuals
Heavy reliance on a separate socai CLI and an OpenRouter key

rising.description: 🔎 Username, email & phone OSINT — 9,700+ lookup checks from 19 projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs and expert-reviewed updates.
rising.summary: Consensus is a Python CLI and GUI that runs username, email and phone lookups across about 9,700 site modules from 19 open-source projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs, PDF reports and an MCP server for AI assistants.
strengths: Large consolidated module set with a stated review process
Windows installer, PyPI package and source install options
Evidence graph and PDF reporting for investigations
risks: Mass username and email lookups can enable profiling of private individuals
Claims of weekly expert review are unverified marketing

rising.description: An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view — and shows its work. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.
rising.summary: An agent skill that geolocates photos by combining EXIF and OCR, reverse image search, OpenStreetMap corridors, elevation skylines, sun position, satellite and street-view matching, and reports its reasoning as evidence.
strengths: Clear multi-stage pipeline with named scripts and data sources
Shows its work with evidence overlays
Works across several agent platforms with setup instructions
risks: Geolocating photos may be misused to locate private places or people
Depends on Chrome/Chromium and external services for reverse image search

rising.description: Wireshark for the radio spectrum: channelize a wide span once, decode every signal in it at once
rising.summary: Desktop SDR tool that channelizes a wide radio band and decodes many signal types at once, including ISM devices, ADS-B, AIS, APRS, pagers, DMR, TETRA, LoRa and radiosondes, with recording and an agent option.
strengths: Decodes many protocols from one wide-band capture
Named decoders and bands with a clear install path
Passive reception of public transmissions
risks: Intercepting TETRA and DMR traffic with decryption and key recovery raises legal concerns
Records voice and messages, which may capture private communications
Agent can transmit on radio, requiring licensing awareness

rising.description: Continuously updated catalogue of open-source OSINT tools, skills, plugins, MCP servers, and agentic integrations.
rising.summary: A continuously updated, hand-reviewed catalogue of open-source OSINT tools, MCP servers, agent skills and agentic integrations, organised by category and by target input, with a CSV database.
strengths: Large, categorised catalogue of roughly 495 projects
Browsable by target input and by category
Provides a CSV database and emerging/agentic subsets
risks: Catalogue quality depends on maintenance; last update timestamp is recent but unverified
Listing tools does not itself vet their legal or ethical use

rising.description: Watchdog (branding subject to change) is an open-source intelligence (OSINT) case management platform for small teams.
rising.summary: Open-source case management platform for small OSINT teams. Lookup results are held as proposals that a person must accept before entering the case graph, with export regenerated from the graph. Pre-1.0.
strengths: Human-in-the-loop acceptance of machine results supports defensible provenance
Clear architecture and stack documentation with CI and coverage badges
risks: Pre-1.0 with schemas and API shapes changing without notice
Not hardened for multi-tenant or production deployment

rising.description: Scrape Facebook GraphQL data without an API key — profiles, posts, comments, reactions, groups, marketplace, search_engine.
rising.summary: Python library that scrapes Facebook data via internal GraphQL endpoints using exported session cookies, covering profiles, posts, comments, reactions, groups and marketplace, with automatic Doc ID rediscovery via V8.
strengths: Documented Python API with concrete examples
Uses GraphQL endpoints instead of brittle HTML parsing
Documentation site linked
risks: Uses user session cookies, which may violate Facebook terms of service
Lead-generation framing and profile extraction raise privacy concerns
Relies on unofficial endpoints that may break

rising.description: High-Performance Wayback Machine CDX Recon & Triage Workspace for Chrome (Manifest V3). Stream archived URLs, rank by security risk, verify live 200s, and export.
rising.summary: Chrome Manifest V3 extension that streams Wayback Machine CDX archived URLs, ranks them by security risk (.env, keys, .git, SQL dumps), mines parameters, verifies live 200s, and exports results.
strengths: Concrete features: streaming CDX parsing, risk tiers, live HEAD verification
Runs locally as an unpacked extension with clear install steps
Zero-tracking privacy stance stated
risks: Security-recon framing leans toward attack-surface work with bug-bounty and fuzzing emphasis
Some README claims are marketing-style (High-Performance, Zero Tracking badges)

rising.description: Open-source intelligence and human-rights hub on North Korea: intel map, missile test explorer, leadership graph, camps and verified data.
rising.summary: Open-source hub on North Korea combining an intel map with prison camps, missile tests, satellite-derived layers, sanctions data and sourced datasets, plus a weekly source-refresh workflow. Human-rights oriented.
strengths: Sourced datasets with weekly automated refresh
Satellite imagery layers with stated time coverage
Open data and Apache 2.0 license
risks: Advocacy framing may affect neutrality of data selection
Primarily a website; little detail on methodology in the excerpt

rising.description: Free alternative to https://osint-ui.com
rising.summary: A free, browser-based suite of about 20 OSINT tools covering username, email, breach, password-hash, DNS and certificate lookups, with a FastAPI backend for some tools. Positioned as a free alternative to osint-ui.com.
strengths: Many tools with named free public data sources
Browser-first design keeps analysed files local
Explicit passive-only stance and documented data sources
risks: Username and email lookups can support personal-data inference
Licence combines Apache 2.0 with Commons Clause, limiting commercial use
Readme digest is truncated, so some tool details are unverified

rising.description: ⚒️ Open-source OSINT and digital forensics skills for AI assistants. Investigate sources, challenge hypotheses, analyze artifacts, and produce evidence-referenced reports with portable case files and offline Python tools. Designed for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI.
rising.summary: A set of 16 agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI that turn sources and artifacts into portable case files with preserved evidence, referenced findings, and offline Python tools.
strengths: Preserves originals with byte checks and source references
Offline Python runtime with stated limits and no telemetry
Multiple export formats including GraphML and EN/FR reports
risks: Reliance on host assistant for web research and model data transmission
Recorded trials do not establish accuracy gains, per the README

rising.description: OmniScope Web - 100% Serverless Static Geospatial Intelligence & Doppler Weather Radar Dashboard for Cloudflare Pages. Zero cloud database fees, zero server costs, pure open data.
rising.summary: Serverless static dashboard for Cloudflare Pages that displays live weather radar, USGS earthquake feeds, Open-Meteo weather data, public webcams and ISS orbit tracking, with an MCP server and keyless edge APIs.
strengths: Keyless, serverless design using open CORS-enabled data sources
Clear list of named data sources
Offers MCP and REST access
risks: Heavy self-promotional and trademark language with unverifiable claims like certified 147-model consensus
Primarily weather and space data rather than investigative OSINT
Warns of clones while asserting unverifiable authority

rising.description: Multi-agent open-source intelligence and threat analysis platform with source attribution, evidence provenance, and encrypted credential storage.
rising.summary: Next.js/TypeScript OSINT platform that harvests public sources such as DNS, certificate logs, registries, sanctions lists and blockchain explorers, hashes evidence with SHA-256, and runs multi-agent hypothesis analysis with citation checks.
strengths: Documents concrete data sources and known limitations
Evidence hashing and source citation validation support auditability
Explicit ethical use boundaries prohibiting doxxing and harassment
risks: Heavy marketing language in README (zero-hallucination claims) without independent validation
Reliance on LLM-generated analysis despite guardrail claims
Single-node SQLite persistence limits production use

rising.description: An OSINT investigation case mapping tool for organizing entities, relationships, evidence, and intelligence.
rising.summary: A local, offline investigation case tool for profiling subjects, mapping link networks with shortest path and centrality, placing locations on a map, building timelines, storing evidence with an audit log, and exporting PDF or HTML reports.
strengths: Runs locally with no server or telemetry
Concrete features: link network analysis, timeline, evidence vault with audit log
Install options and sample case reports provided
risks: Subject profiling of individuals could be misused for personal data collection
Limited detail on data sources and legal considerations

rising.description: A responsible, open-source Instagram username availability scanner. Async CLI with bounded concurrency, rate-limit backoff, resumable scans, Docker and GitHub Actions support.
rising.summary: Async Python CLI that generates short Instagram usernames and checks public profile pages to flag names with no visible profile. Supports rate-limit backoff, resumable scans, and txt, json, or csv output. Results are candidates only and must be verified on Instagram.
strengths: Documents clear limitations and that results are not guaranteed claimable
Resumable checkpoints and conservative UNKNOWN classification
Concrete example run and multiple output formats
risks: Brute-force enumeration of platform accounts may conflict with Instagram terms of service
Usefulness for OSINT is limited; mainly a username availability tool
Scope is contestable since the purpose is registration availability rather than investigation

rising.description: Instagram Scraper — free, open-source Instagram scraper. Unlimited profiles, posts, reels, comments and hashtags as clean JSON, no API key, no proxies.
rising.summary: A Python API that scrapes public Instagram profiles, posts, reels, comments and hashtags into JSON, run locally via a FastAPI-style server with 19 endpoints. Marketed as free and unlimited.
strengths: Runnable local API with a curl example
Clear endpoint coverage for profiles, posts, comments and hashtags
Open-source and installable from requirements
risks: Scrapes personal profile data and email addresses, raising privacy concerns
Marketing claims of unlimited data without stated limits or legal considerations
Likely to break against Instagram changes; bundled promotional content

rising.description: Self-scan CLI that shows what an attacker can build from your own public data. Keyless, read-only, local-first.
rising.summary: A keyless, read-only CLI that verifies ownership of an email address, then gathers public traces (accounts, leaks, photo GPS, git identity) about you and builds a local profile and report. An optional mode generates a simulated phishing email and a non-submitting login page.

Documents its collectors, public sources and read-only design in a clear table
Local-first with no API keys or cloud dependency

Person-level lookup tool that could be pointed at others despite the self-scan framing

rising.description: Check simultaneously if a phone number is registered on popular apps & websites, without any prerequisite 📞
rising.summary: Go CLI and TUI that checks in parallel whether a phone number is registered on several popular apps and websites. Offers JSON output, privacy-conscious logging, and a single-target scope.
strengths: Concrete CLI usage with parallel module checks and JSON output
Privacy-conscious logging and silent-by-default modules
Cross-platform binaries and go install path
risks: Phone-number registration checks can enable targeting of private individuals
Installation section is partly unfinished (work-in-progress notes)
Legal section relies on a non-OSI internal-use license

rising.description: GeoWeb — find where any photo (or video) was taken. A local-first, open-source browser console around the GeoInt recon pipeline, with Docker, docs and a GitHub Pages landing site.
rising.summary: GeoWeb is a local-first browser console that analyses photos and videos to estimate where they were taken, combining EXIF metadata, OCR, reverse image search, object detection, camera calibration and learned world priors, with an interactive map and MCP server support.
strengths: Runs locally with no upload of evidence
Shows evidence and caveats so the analyst makes the final call
Documented quickstart, Docker setup and demo sessions
risks: Reverse image search results and learned priors may be wrong without analyst verification
Young project with limited history evident from the digest

rising.description: Track the flights that carry weapons. Free, open-source flight search, live map and AI research assistant for journalists. In memory of Sha'ban al-Dalou.
rising.summary: SADA is a free open-source tool that searches a multi-year ADS-B flight archive, with an AI assistant, live map and documented weapons-shipment cases, to help journalists trace flights carrying arms.

Explicit guidance on reading observed versus inferred flights and on what the data cannot show
risks: Flight-tracking of state arms transfers could be contested politically; findings need careful verification
Reliance on paid OpenRouter or Anthropic keys for the assistant

rising.description: Terminal-first GitHub public-footprint inspection tool
rising.summary: Rust CLI and HTTP service that inspects public GitHub profiles, repositories, commit identities and SSH keys, producing JSON, Markdown, text, SVG or PDF reports with source references and caveats about inferred data.

Privacy and limitations section and explicit distinction of observed vs inferred data
Does not execute code from inspected repositories
risks: Aggregates personal commit email addresses and activity timezone inferences about individuals
Optional GitLeak enrichment touches leaked-data sources

rising.description: Real-time tactical OSINT & GEOINT dashboard. Live flight tracking (ADS-B), maritime vessels, satellites, undersea telecom cables & HUD shaders powered by free, keyless open APIs.
rising.summary: Open-source tactical dashboard showing live ADS-B aircraft, AIS vessels, satellites, public traffic cameras, earthquakes, and undersea cables on 2D and 3D maps, using free keyless APIs.
strengths: Named public data sources with endpoints listed
Keyless, runnable locally with clear quick-start steps
Explicit disclaimer and honest labelling of non-live data
risks: Marketing-heavy README with some unsupported superlatives
Limited detail on legal considerations for camera feed aggregation

rising.description: Local-first digital image forensics & pixel analysis workbench with 44 registered inspection modules.
rising.summary: A local-first Flask web app that inspects image pixels, statistics, bit planes, compression clues (such as ELA) and metadata to surface candidate anomalies for manual digital investigation, with HTML and PDF reports.

Broad set of named forensic modules with clear setup instructions
Includes automated tests and CI

rising.description: 28 OSINT Agent Skills that turn Cursor, Claude & AI coding agents into a full open-source intelligence platform — reconnaissance, attribution, GEOINT, breach checks & due diligence. Ethical, sourced, passive-first.
rising.summary: A set of 28 agent skills for Cursor and Claude that chain OSINT techniques such as WHOIS, DNS, certificate transparency, breach lookups, reverse image search and geolocation into sourced reports. Includes install script and reference material.
strengths: Broad coverage across OSINT domains with 10 workflows and 18 techniques
Emphasises passive-first methodology and sourced, confidence-rated findings
Includes install script and reference cookbooks

Marketing-heavy README with illustrative rather than verified example output

Structured output with permalinks and dates for verification

strengths: Clear public-only limits and caveats stated in README
Runnable usage examples and defined outputs

Named sources and tools (googlenewsdecoder, trafilatura)
Auditable daily Markdown output

established.description: OSINT toolkit for crypto investigations: trace stolen funds on Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron and Solana — CLI and local web UI

Documents honest limitations such as pseudonymity and mixers

Clear multi-stage pipeline with documented sources and evidence per candidate
Explicit ethical-use section

Dual-use potential for locating people from photos

Concrete features: entity taxonomy, Admiralty source grading, .trace export
Multilingual UI and offline and 100% local modes

Tests and badges are self-reported; no independent verification of claims

established.description: Offline desktop workspace for organizing OSINT investigations.

strengths: Fully offline with no telemetry or accounts
Visual investigation board with relationships and exports
Tests in CI on Windows and Ubuntu
risks: Early-stage project with limited documentation of data formats
Binary release targets Windows x64 only

Documents data sources such as the IEEE registry and primary sources
Works on phone alone with a published signed APK
risks: Tracker and public-safety matching could be used to track individuals' devices or police presence
Signature matching can produce false positives, as the README itself notes

Runs locally with inspectable source and no required API keys
risks: Localization fork of an upstream project; content largely mirrors original
CCTV poses and launch trajectories are described as coarse estimates

Multiple export formats and persistent SQLite storage

Multiple outputs including SARIF for code scanning

web-capture.summary: SimpleReconDorking runs search dorks in parallel across multiple search engines and returns the union of found URLs. Supports dork strings, files, a built-in categorised catalogue, and stdin, with Docker install and usage examples.
strengths: Clear purpose and multiple input modes
Documented usage examples and Docker setup
Built-in dork catalogue by category
risks: Dorking can be used to find exposed targets; README carries a consent warning only
Some engines require browser bypass, which may violate terms of service

web-capture.summary: Python client that queries a CIRCL-hosted Common Crawl index service to search archived web pages by URL, hostname, FQDN or digest, and retrieves only the selected WARC byte ranges. Access requires a token issued by CIRCL on request.
strengths: Queries metadata index before fetching, avoiding full crawl downloads
Documents multiple search modes and output formats with examples
risks: Depends on a token-gated third-party service with discretionary access
Access controls and README sample commands are partially truncated

web-capture.description: Ferramenta de extração e descoberta de URLs para fluxos de OSINT e reconhecimento
web-capture.summary: Python CLI that takes seed URLs, fetches pages and passive/active sources to extract and discover reachable URLs, with optional same-origin spidering, recursive rounds, Docker support and API-key-based sources.
strengths: Clear purpose for URL discovery in recon workflows
Supports passive and active sources, crawling and Docker
Documents usage flags, profiles and presets
risks: Active probing of target sites may raise authorisation concerns
Readme digest shows template-like source examples, limited detail on data sources

web-capture.description: GOBLIN TSUNAMI - OSINT framework generating 400+ Google Dorks across Instagram, Threads, Facebook & TikTok. Advanced digital footprint analysis with 25+ tracking categories for cybersecurity professionals, threat intelligence, and ethical reconnaissance operations.
web-capture.summary: Python framework that generates large sets of Google dork queries targeting Instagram, Threads, Facebook and TikTok to map an individual's digital footprint across tracking categories. README is mostly marketing with little concrete usage detail.
strengths: Clear dork-generation purpose across four platforms
Install instructions provided
risks: Targets individuals' digital footprints, enabling person tracking and location profiling
Heavy marketing language with few concrete examples or limits
Placeholder links and repository URLs suggest unfinished project

workspace-analysis.description: Watchdog (branding subject to change) is an open-source intelligence (OSINT) case management platform for small teams.
workspace-analysis.summary: Open-source case management platform for small OSINT teams. Lookup results are held as proposals that a person must accept before entering the case graph, with export regenerated from the graph. Pre-1.0.
strengths: Human-in-the-loop acceptance of machine results supports defensible provenance
Clear architecture and stack documentation with CI and coverage badges
risks: Pre-1.0 with schemas and API shapes changing without notice
Not hardened for multi-tenant or production deployment

workspace-analysis.description: An OSINT investigation case mapping tool for organizing entities, relationships, evidence, and intelligence.
workspace-analysis.summary: A local, offline investigation case tool for profiling subjects, mapping link networks with shortest path and centrality, placing locations on a map, building timelines, storing evidence with an audit log, and exporting PDF or HTML reports.
strengths: Runs locally with no server or telemetry
Concrete features: link network analysis, timeline, evidence vault with audit log
Install options and sample case reports provided
risks: Subject profiling of individuals could be misused for personal data collection
Limited detail on data sources and legal considerations

workspace-analysis.description: Collaborative peer-to-peer OSINT investigation board — end-to-end encrypted, no server-side data, works offline. Desktop app for Windows & Linux.
workspace-analysis.summary: COSINT is an offline-capable, peer-to-peer desktop investigation board for Windows and Linux. Analysts map entities, link them, grade sources, and collaborate in real time with end-to-end encryption and no server-side storage.
strengths: Clear architecture with E2E encrypted P2P sync and no backend
Concrete features: entity taxonomy, Admiralty source grading, .trace export
Multilingual UI and offline and 100% local modes
risks: Mostly case-management tooling rather than data collection
Tests and badges are self-reported; no independent verification of claims

workspace-analysis.description: Terminal-first local OSINT field workbench with rigorous evidence provenance. Cases, content-addressed evidence, origin clustering, contradiction candidates, honest tool catalogue. Local-first, no telemetry.
workspace-analysis.summary: A terminal-first local OSINT workbench that stores collected evidence as hash-addressed copies under scoped cases, tracks claims and relations with analyst review, clusters origins, flags contradictions, and exports integrity-checkable bundles.
strengths: Content-addressed evidence verifiable with sha256sum
Clear limitations and status tracking
Local-first with no telemetry
risks: Alpha pre-release with small username provider set
TUI experimental
Catalogue entries lack adapters yet

workspace-analysis.description: Offline desktop workspace for organizing OSINT investigations.
workspace-analysis.summary: OpenTrace is an offline Windows/Linux desktop app (PySide6) for organizing OSINT investigations with a visual board, tasks, sources, hypotheses, journal, SHA-256 integrity info, and portable case folders. No telemetry or accounts.
strengths: Fully offline with no telemetry or accounts
Visual investigation board with relationships and exports
Tests in CI on Windows and Ubuntu
risks: Early-stage project with limited documentation of data formats
Binary release targets Windows x64 only

workspace-analysis.description: Open source alternative of Palantir Gotham  🌟 Star if you like it! 🌟'
workspace-analysis.summary: Open-source intelligence integration and link-analysis platform meant as an alternative to Palantir Gotham, with ontology-driven data fusion, graph visualization, GIS mapping, timelines and an AI co-pilot. Much of the described functionality is planned rather than implemented.
strengths: Clear purpose as a Gotham-style analysis workspace
Backend and frontend setup steps given
risks: Heavy marketing language with little concrete detail on data sources
Many features listed as planned rather than working
Defense and law enforcement targeting without stated legal safeguards
